recipes.name: Caribbean Holiday Shrimp
ingredients_raw: 2 pounds large cooked shrimp, peeled, tails on

steps.text: In a large bowl combine oil, ginger, lime juice, garlic, soy sauce, sugar and red pepper; mix well. Stir in shrimp and cilantro. Cover and refrigerate 1 to 4 hours before serving. Stir occasionally while chilling.

raw_recipe.headline: Caribbean Holiday Shrimp
raw_recipe.description: Cooked shrimp marinated in ginger, lime juice, garlic, soy sauce and cilantro.
raw_recipe.name: Caribbean Holiday Shrimp
recipeIngredient: 2 pounds large cooked shrimp, peeled, tails on

recipeInstructions.text: In a large bowl combine oil, ginger, lime juice, garlic, soy sauce, sugar and red pepper; mix well. Stir in shrimp and cilantro. Cover and refrigerate 1 to 4 hours before serving. Stir occasionally while chilling.

review.reviewBody: This shrimp recipe is really wonderful! Very easy to make - definately let it sit at least four hours as recipe says - also rinse shrimp off and pat dry before starting (I know this is common sense, but I totally forgot to do this the first time and it does make a difference!)

I prepared these this morning and we ate them as an appetizer before dinner so they had plenty of time to marinate. The marinade was good but you probably want to cook your own shrimp so you can add seasoning (like Old Bay or Shrimp Better-Than-Boullion) to the cooking process. The store-bought cooked shrimp were tasteless and no amount of marinade could overcome the unseasoned cooked shrimp.

We really enjoyed this dish and can't wait to make it again. I put the shrimp on small kabobs sticks with cherry tomatoes and the presentation was so pretty and the flavors were outstanding. I did not use the red pepper flakes but put in 1/2 tsp of hot sauce and it blended very well. After plating I sprinkled a little more cilantro over it for color. I took this to a friend house and she would not let me leave until I gave her the recipe. :-)

Based from some of the reviews, I used one lime and brown sugar instead of white. This marinated for six hours. I tossed it in a salad, using baby spinach, a little finely sliced red onion, a small chopped bell pepper and some shredded carrot. The marinade was used as the dressing. Everyone loved this, there were no leftovers. Thanks, Sue for sharing.

So good! Made a double batch for an office beach party, followed the recipe, except I used frozen cooked shrimp. Defrosted them in the microwave, turning them frequently and sprinkling Old Bay Seasoning on them each time. They were delicious.

I received rave reviews for this Caribbean Shrimp dish. I added more garlic - used 3 to 4 cloves instead of 2. Also, I only used the cilantro as a garnish for an elegant presentation. I will be making it again and again! Thank you for sharing this delish recipe!
This was really good, though i halved the quantity of ginger/pepper and oil and used basil leaves to garnish, next time i will try and use mint leaves for the garnish.

This is the best marinade for shrimp we have ever had! Like others, we only marinated for 30-40 minutes and then threw into an aluminum foil packet and grilled for 5 minutes. The only thing we changed was (and I hate when people change it),but we substituted dried cilantro. And, as always, more garlic!
We are passing this on to our entire family and will use again and again. Thanks so much! We are thrilled with this recipe!

Delicious. I served hot right off the grill, the biggest hit of my BBQ. They tasted great cooked over some alder wood chips to give it a tiny bit of sweet smokey flavor. My only critique, just a tiny bit much lime and sugar... i'm not a big sweet n sour guy, so next time I'll half the sugar and use just a few tablespoons lime juice. Otherwise, fantastic.

I only used one lb. of shrimp but made all the marinade so that I would have enough to use as a dressing on our salad. I added just a bit of brown sugar because the lime seemed a bit strong. Also, I cut back on the ginger but I felt it was still too much...next time I will only use a tbp., if that. Marinaded them for about 5 hours & served them on top of a bed of spring greens w/ sliced cucumbers. Served the salad w/ mango slices on the side & for dessert, Coconut Lime Sorbet (from this site). Was an extremely quick, extremely healthy, very tasty meal...thanks!

This was a wonderful, quick and easy appetizer. We purchased the large cooked deveined with tails on shrimp in a bag and poured the marinade directly into the recloseable bags that the shrimp came in. Very good reviews!

Made this awesome dish for christmas dinner last year and it was a hit! My family loved it and its now the second item im supposed to make for the holidays...especially this coming Thanksgiving and Christmas dinner ^_^

This is a great recipe! Everyone at the party loved it and couldn’t stop talking about it. It couldn’t have been easier to throw together. I added extra lime juice so it was a bit more citrus tasting and bright but otherwise kept everything else the same. Will definitely make again!
went over very well at holiday party

My wife and I thought this was great. Very 'fresh' taste with the lime, ginger and cilantro flavors. Based on others' comments, I cut the ginger in half. I actually think a bit more ginger would have been better. I used the full amount of red pepper flakes and found it only mildly spicy. So this is probably a matter of taste and maybe how fresh your red pepper flakes are. I used frozen, pre-cooked shrimp, peeled with tails on. Made this a real easy recipe to make. With the full flavor of the marinade, I didn't think it was worth the trouble of fresh shrimp.
So Gooooood and Easy! Made it for a dinner party and it was a hit. So I made it again a few days later for another dinner party. Hit again. Will definitely be using this recipe again.

I made this for our Christmas appetizer. I made the marinade the night before and added the shrimp in the morning. I let marinade for 4 hours. This lacked something but I'm not sure what. The marinade bece watery when I added the shrimp even tho I let sit on a paper towel before adding to the marinade. I used then entire amount of crushed pepper and followed the recipe to the T but it still lacked something to the point we broke out our St. Elmo's cocktail sauce and put it on the shrimp. That gave it the kick it needed. I don't think I'll make this again just because I like the marinade to really pop instead of just being another shrimp cocktail dish.
I made this for a Caribbean themed dinner party and it was amazing! Definitely a keeper. I followed the recipe exactly, with a little less cilantro than called for. My guests loved it too.
We added rice and green beans and enjoyed it as a meal
Fantastic!!! Used for a couple of parties and everyone loved them.
